summary: This PIB backgrounder consolidates India's cultural heritage initiatives, covering monument conservation schemes (Adopt a Heritage 2.0, PRASHAD, Swadesh Darshan), ASI's protection of 3,686 monuments, repatriation of antiquities including the Piprahwa Buddha relics, digitisation missions like Gyan Bharatam and National Manuscript Survey, AI-based language preservation tools (BHASHINI, Adi-Vaani), and India's 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites. It presents cumulative statistics and achievements across multiple ministries as of 2025-2026.

title: LOKAYAN 2026 - INDIAN NAVAL SHIP SUDARSHINI ENTERS PONTA DELGADA, PORTUGAL
summary: INS Sudarshini, the Indian Navy's sail training ship, arrived at Ponta Delgada, Azores (Portugal) on 13 August 2026, completing a 19-day transoceanic Atlantic crossing from Boston, USA, as part of the Lokayan 2026 voyage. This marks the ship's second Atlantic crossing, and it has covered over 15,000 nautical miles so far, engaging in goodwill and cultural exchange activities with the Portuguese Navy.

title: APEDA and Government of Tripura Organise International Organic Buyer-Seller Meet to Expand Global Market Linkages
summary: APEDA, in collaboration with the Tripura State Organic Farming Development Agency and the state Agriculture Department, organised an International Organic Buyer-Seller Meet in Agartala on 14 August 2026 to connect Tripura's organic farmers and exporters with global buyers. Around 200 participants attended, including over 20 international buyers from countries like Australia, Germany and Argentina, 27 exporters, and 96 farmers from 22 FPOs/FPCs, showcasing products such as Queen Pineapple and GI-tagged Kalikhasa Rice. The event aimed to build market linkages and boost export opportunities for the state's organic produce.

title: Logistics Data Bank Tracks 10 Crore EXIM Containers, Provides Visibility across Logistics Chain
summary: The Logistics Data Bank (LDB), a digital tracking platform launched in 2016, has tracked 10 crore EXIM containers using RFID-based technology across 19 ports, 32 container terminals and other logistics nodes nationwide. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal called this a milestone in India's logistics journey, emphasising technology's role in improving efficiency and industrial competitiveness. The platform, operated by NICDC Logistics Data Services Limited (NLDSL), was upgraded to LDB 2.0 in September 2025 to include high-seas tracking and multimodal shipment visibility.

title: TRAI assesses mobile network quality across Shimla & Solan and nearby areas under HP LSA, during the month of June 2026
summary: TRAI released findings of an Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted in June 2026 across Shimla, Solan and adjoining areas in Himachal Pradesh's HP Licensed Service Area, assessing mobile voice and data quality of four telecom operators (Airtel, BSNL, Reliance Jio, Vodafone Idea). The report measured parameters like coverage gaps, call drop rates, call silence instances, and data download/upload speeds across city, highway, hotspot and walk-test routes, with Jio and Airtel generally showing better 5G speeds and lower drop rates than BSNL and VIL.

title: Electronics Hardware Technology Parks Strengthen India’s Export Oriented Electronics Manufacturing Ecosystem
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply on 12 August 2026, the Minister of State for Electronics and IT stated that the number of Electronics Hardware Technology Park (EHTP) units rose from 70 in FY 2023-24 to 79 in FY 2025-26, with exports estimated at ₹11,102 crore in FY 2025-26, up from ₹9,678 crore in FY 2023-24. Karnataka accounts for the largest share of units (34) and exports (₹8,329 crore), followed by Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh. The EHTP scheme is a 100% export-oriented scheme with no dedicated fund allocation, administered by STPI through single-window statutory clearances.

title: Government Strengthens Cyber Security Preparedness of Central Government Digital Platforms and Citizen Services
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply on 12 August 2026, MoS Electronics & IT Jitin Prasada detailed India's cyber security architecture for government digital platforms, citing CERT-In as the statutory nodal incident response agency under Section 70B of the IT Act. He noted cyber incidents rose from 15,92,917 in 2023 to 20,41,360 in 2024 to 29,44,248 in 2025, and listed institutional mechanisms including NCSC, NCCC, NCIIPC, sectoral CSIRTs (Finance, Power), Cyber Swachhta Kendra, and awareness/training programmes under ISEA and CERT-In.

title: Chips to Start-ups Programme Strengthens India’s Semiconductor Design Ecosystem and Industry Ready Talent
summary: In response to a Lok Sabha question on 12 August 2026, MoS Electronics & IT Jitin Prasada informed Parliament that under the Chips to Start-ups (C2S) Programme, over 68,000 students have been trained against a target of 85,000 industry-ready professionals in semiconductor chip design. The programme has provided 332 academic institutions across India access to advanced Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools, and participating institutions have successfully taped out 254 chip designs (175 at 180nm node at SCL Mohali, 79 at overseas foundries). Andhra Pradesh alone has 23 institutions with EDA access and four funded research projects on RISC-V processors, hardware accelerators, neuromorphic processors, and AI co-processing units.

title: NHRC, India takessuo motucognizance of reported death of 19 CRPF personnel between January to May 2026, as per the official data compiled by CRPF
summary: The NHRC has taken suo motu cognizance of media reports that 19 CRPF personnel died by suicide between January and 22 May 2026, following data showing the force recorded 59 suicides in 2025 — the highest in five years. It has issued notices to the Union Home Secretary and CRPF Director General seeking a detailed report within two weeks. Reports indicate 281 CRPF personnel died by suicide over the last five years (2021-2025), of which about 216 were on duty.

title: Creating a new milestone in the policy of zero tolerance against narcotics, NCB secures the return of fugitive drug kingpin Virender Singh Basoya from the UAE
summary: The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) brought back fugitive drug trafficker Virender Singh Basoya to India from the UAE, where he had been arrested in June 2026 following an INTERPOL Red Notice sought by NCB. Basoya is linked to a Pune-origin Mephedrone trafficking case involving recoveries of about 1,837 kg of the drug, as well as a separate Delhi Police Special Cell cocaine-trafficking cartel case with over 1,300 kg of seizures. His return is presented as part of NCB's 'Operation GLOBAL-HUNT' and the government's 'Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029)'.

title: NHRC, India takessuo motucognizance of the reported death of one person and injuries to another after inhaling toxic gases while cleaning a manhole at a factory in Faridabad district, Haryana
summary: The NHRC took suo motu cognizance of a media report that on 11 August 2026, one person died and another was injured after inhaling toxic gases while cleaning a manhole without safety equipment at a factory in Sector-25, Faridabad, Haryana. The Commission issued notices to the Haryana Chief Secretary and Faridabad Police Commissioner seeking a detailed report within two weeks, covering the investigation status, the injured worker's health, and compensation provided to him and the deceased's next of kin.

title: NHRC, India takessuo motucognizance of the reported snake bite of six girls leading to three deaths in a hostel in Gadchiroli district, Maharashtra
summary: The NHRC has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that six Scheduled Tribe girl students were bitten by a snake at an Ashram school hostel in Gadchiroli district, Maharashtra, after being forced to sleep on the floor due to lack of cots; three of them died. The Commission issued a notice to the Maharashtra Chief Secretary seeking a detailed report within two weeks, including the health status of the injured, noting the report indicated 79 girls were housed in a single room in a 25-year-old hostel lacking basic facilities.

title: PROVISIONAL ESTIMATES OF WHOLESALE PRICE INDEX, OUTPUT PRODUCER PRICE INDEX, AND TRIAL INPUT PRODUCER PRICE INDEX FOR THE MONTH OF JULY 2026, AND FINAL INDEX FOR THE MONTH OF MAY 2026
summary: The Ministry of Commerce & Industry released provisional Wholesale Price Index (WPI, Base Year 2022-23) data for July 2026, showing WPI inflation at 9.78% year-on-year, marginally down from 9.87% in June 2026. Primary Articles inflation rose to 8.52%, while Fuel and Power inflation fell sharply to 20.05% from 27.41%, and Manufactured Products inflation rose to 8.29%. The Food Index recorded 6.65% YoY inflation, and the final WPI for May 2026 was revised upward from 9.68% (provisional) to 9.88%.

title: Software Technology Parks Strengthen India’s IT Export Ecosystem and Ease of Doing Business
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply dated 12 August 2026, the Minister of Electronics and IT informed Parliament that Software Technology Park (STP) units recorded exports of over ₹7.73 lakh crore in FY 2025-26, up from ₹6.88 lakh crore in FY 2024-25. The number of registered STP units rose to 2,125 in FY 2025-26, with Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra leading in both unit count and export value. The release also listed ease-of-doing-business measures taken by STPI, including automation of SOFTEX filing, integration with RBI's EDPMS system, blanket import permissions, and self-declaration for DTA sales.

title: FutureSkills PRIME Strengthens India’s Future Ready Digital Workforce Through Skilling in Emerging Technologies
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply on 12 August 2026, the IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw provided details on FutureSkills PRIME (FSP), a MeitY-NASSCOM joint skilling programme in emerging technologies. Over 34 lakh candidates have registered on the FSP portal, 23 lakh+ enrolled/trained, and 13 lakh+ certified, with 41% women and 86% from Tier-2/3 cities. The reply also detailed state-wise enrollment data, five-year fund allocation figures, and coverage in the North East and Himalayan region including NIELIT's role and the IndiaAI Mission's Data and AI Labs.

title: PM Vishwakarma Beneficiaries Invited as ‘Special Guests’ to Witness 80th Independence Day Ceremony at Red Fort, Delhi
summary: The Government of India has invited 100 PM Vishwakarma scheme beneficiaries from Delhi-NCR, including women artisans, as 'Special Guests' to witness the 80th Independence Day ceremony at Red Fort on 15 August 2026. They will be felicitated with souvenirs and interact with MSME Ministry officials on 14 August at the Indian Institute of Public Administration, Delhi.

title: 1057 Personnel of Police, Fire, Home Guard & Civil Defence and Correctional Services awarded Gallantry/Service Medals on the occasion of the Independence Day- 2026
summary: On Independence Day 2026, 1057 personnel from Police, Fire, Home Guard & Civil Defence, and Correctional Services were awarded Gallantry and Service Medals. This includes 301 Medals for Gallantry (272 Police, 29 Fire), 92 President's Medals for Distinguished Service, and 664 Medals for Meritorious Service. Among gallantry awardees, 197 were from Left Wing Extremism-affected areas, 51 from Jammu & Kashmir, 12 from the North-East, and 41 from other regions.

title: Prime Minister recalls the courage of those impacted by Partition on Partition Horrors Remembrance Day
summary: On 14 August 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi issued a statement and social media posts marking Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, paying tribute to those affected by the 1947 Partition. He praised their resilience in rebuilding lives and contributing to the nation, and shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam on the value of hard work and human effort over fatalism.

title: DRI busts illegal drug manufacturing facility in Jewar, UP; 30 kg drugs seized and two persons arrested
summary: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) dismantled a clandestine drug manufacturing facility operating from a residential premises in Jewar, Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh, in an operation conducted on 9-10 August 2026. About 30 kg of Amphetamine/intermediary forms, 30 kg of precursor chemicals, and full manufacturing equipment were seized, and a foreign national and his Indian associate were arrested under the NDPS Act, 1985. This is part of a broader DRI crackdown, with three other clandestine facilities busted in Gujarat and Maharashtra in the preceding month.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Milestone achieved in global climate action

ministry.name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

summary: India informed Rajya Sabha that it has achieved a 37.38% reduction in GDP emissions intensity (2022 vs 2005 base) against a 45% NDC target by 2030, and reached 54.18% non-fossil fuel installed electric capacity by June 2026, surpassing 50% in June 2025 — five years ahead of schedule. India also created an additional carbon sink of 2.44 billion tonnes CO2 equivalent (2005-2022) against a 2.5-3.0 billion tonne target by 2030. The NDC targets for 2035 have been enhanced to 47% emissions intensity reduction, 60% non-fossil installed capacity, and 3.5-4.0 billion tonnes carbon sink.

title: Government Strengthens Welfare, Healthcare and Social Security Measures for Senior Citizens
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment detailed government measures for senior citizens' welfare, healthcare and social security amid India's rapidly ageing population, projected to grow from 10 crore (2011) to 23 crore (2036). Key schemes include AVYAY (umbrella scheme), Elderline helpline, Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, SAGE, NPHCE, AB-PMJAY (₹5 lakh cover for 70+), and NSAP pensions, with beneficiary data for 2023-24 to 2025-26.

title: Transforming Education through Smart Classrooms in SC-Dominated Villages: A Digital Learning Initiative in Kathua, Jammu and Kashmir
summary: Under the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY), District Kathua in Jammu and Kashmir has established Smart Classrooms in Government Schools in SC-dominated villages, including border villages Chack Chabba and Chack Nathal and remote Sandhi village in Bani sub-division. Seven classrooms were set up in 2022-23, four more in 2023-24, and three additional in 2025-26, totaling 14 Smart Classrooms equipped with interactive touch panels, furniture, and civil works. The initiative aims to bridge the digital divide and improve learning outcomes for students in remote and border areas.

title: NMBA reaches, sensitizes more than 30.52 crore people across the country, this includes more than 11.87 crore youth and 8.45 crore women
summary: The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment informed the Rajya Sabha that the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) has sensitized over 30.52 crore people nationwide, including 11.87 crore youth and 8.45 crore women, as part of the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR). In Jammu & Kashmir specifically, over 1.20 crore people have been sensitized, supported by a network of treatment facilities including 1 IRCA, 3 ODICs, 2 CPLI programmes, 6 DDACs and 21 Addiction Treatment Facilities, with persons treated rising from 5,382 in 2021-22 to 46,491 in 2025-26.

title: Central Government Reaffirms Measures to Protect Rights and Promote Inclusion of LGBTQAI+ Community
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment detailed multi-ministry measures to protect the rights and promote inclusion of the LGBTQAI+ community, including intersex persons. These cover legal protection under the amended Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019, ration card entitlements for queer partners, joint bank accounts and nominee rights, healthcare access including ban on conversion therapy and sex reassignment surgery availability, and safety/prison visitation advisories from the Ministry of Home Affairs.

title: INDIA AND KENYA SHARE HISTORICAL AND MULTIFACETED RELATIONS GOING BACK OVER MILLENNIA: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
summary: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla met Kenya's National Assembly Speaker Dr. Moses M. Wetang'ula and a visiting Kenyan parliamentary delegation at Parliament House, highlighting historical India-Kenya ties and growing parliamentary cooperation. Kenya's Speaker reiterated support for India's candidature as a Permanent Member of the UN Security Council and praised India's diaspora contribution to Kenya. Birla welcomed Kenya's decision to recognize Persons of Indian Origin as an indigenous community and noted plans to install a Mahatma Gandhi statue in Kenya's Parliament, alongside continued technical cooperation via PRIDE.

title: Union Minister of Textiles to inaugurate Handloom Haat: The Handloom Experience Centre at Janpath on 14 August
summary: Union Minister of Textiles Giriraj Singh will inaugurate 'Handloom Haat: The Handloom Experience Centre' at Janpath, New Delhi on 14 August 2026, converting the erstwhile handloom retail outlet into a three-floor space combining heritage display, contemporary design and retail. The inaugural showcase includes 24 award-winning weavers curated by the National Handloom Development Corporation (NHDC) and 30+ brands via the fifth edition of 'Weave The Future'. The centre also houses a permanent Visvakarma Gallery showcasing textiles from the 1981-1991 Visvakarma exhibition series and a temporary exhibition on Odisha weaves like Ganjam Bomkai and Dhalapathar Tapestry.

title: Vice President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Meets Parliamentary Delegation from Kenya
summary: Vice President and Rajya Sabha Chairman C. P. Radhakrishnan met a Kenyan Parliamentary Delegation led by Speaker Moses Wetang'ula on 13 August 2026, discussing parliamentary cooperation, digital technology, and India's development partnership with Kenya. He highlighted scholarships, capacity-building programmes, the Digi-Locker pilot project, and GATI Shakti cooperation, while seeking Kenya's support for India's UN Security Council membership and inviting Kenya to join the International Solar Alliance and International Big Cat Alliance.

title: Hon'ble Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment to chair the 5th Meeting of the National Council for Senior Citizens (NCSrC)
summary: Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar will chair the 5th meeting of the National Council for Senior Citizens (NCSrC) at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi, bringing together central and state representatives, MPs, national commissions, experts, and NGOs working on elderly welfare. The Council will discuss key issues concerning senior citizens' welfare to strengthen inter-ministerial convergence in line with the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision. The Ministry will also launch an e-book titled 'SNEHA - Stories of Nurturing, Engagement, Happiness & Active Ageing', documenting achievements of the Senior Citizen Division from October 2024 to June 2026.

title: From Financial Barriers to Engineering Aspirations:
summary: This PIB release is a human-interest story about Prince Yadav, a 19-year-old OBC student from an agricultural family, who is pursuing a B.Tech at MANIT Bhopal. In 2025-26, he received ₹1,15,400 under the PM YASASVI Scholarship, which covered his tuition and hostel expenses, allowing him to avoid taking an educational loan and focus on academics.

title: Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) receives 20 bids under the Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent (REPM)
summary: The Ministry of Heavy Industries received 20 bids through a global tender on the CPP portal for setting up integrated Sintered NdFeB Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM) manufacturing facilities under the Rs. 7,280 crore scheme approved by the Union Cabinet on 26 November 2025. Technical bids were opened on 13 August 2026 in the presence of bidders, following an RFP floated on 20 March 2026. The scheme aims to build 6,000 MTPA of integrated REPM manufacturing capacity in India, to be allocated among five beneficiaries (up to 1,200 MTPA each) over a 7-year period.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF SASCI SCHEME
summary: The Ministry of Tourism informed Rajya Sabha about implementation of the SASCI (Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment) scheme for developing iconic tourist centres. In FY 2024-25, 40 tourism projects across 23 states were sanctioned for ₹3295.76 crore with 100% central funding, evaluated on parameters like connectivity, carrying capacity, and expected tourism/employment impact. In FY 2025-26, under amended guidelines, ₹250 crore each was sanctioned and released to Nagaland, Mizoram, and Himachal Pradesh, states that hadn't availed Part-III funds earlier.

title: Office of Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India Launches the “S&T Cluster Annual Report 2025-2026”

ministry.name: Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI

summary: The Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA) to the Government of India launched the 'S&T Clusters Annual Report 2025-26' on 13 August 2026 under Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, showcasing progress by eight S&T Clusters across India. The report highlights technology translation successes like AI-enabled Digital Podiatry Clinics, indigenous pacemaker components, 3D-printed implants, and platforms like Kalaanubhav.in and i-Passport, alongside growing international collaborations including 12 MoUs from a December 2025 international conference attended by 35+ countries.

title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah hoists the Tricolour at his residence in New Delhi as part of the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign
summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah hoisted the national flag at his residence in New Delhi on 13 August 2026 as part of the 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign. He posted messages on social media describing the campaign as strengthening patriotism and the spirit of 'Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat', and urged citizens to hoist the Tricolour at their homes and upload selfies on the harghartiranga.com portal.

title: Two-day ICMR-SHINE 2026 concludes, igniting scientific curiosity across thousands of young minds

ministry.name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

summary: ICMR concluded the second edition of its nationwide outreach programme 'ICMR-SHINE' (Science & Health Innovation for the Nextgen Explorers) on 11-12 August 2026, covering 83 locations across 31 States and UTs and engaging school students of Classes 9-12 with biomedical and public health research. Highlights included exposure to Mobile BSL-3 laboratories in Nagpur and Gorakhpur, science demonstrations, and a showcase of innovations from Atal Tinkering Labs in Delhi. ICMR also launched a dedicated SHINE website and announced a nationwide school competition on real-world public health challenges, with applications open till 11 September 2026.

title: New computer model can help trace magnetic energy builds up & forecast impact of resulting CMEs
summary: Scientists from the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), along with international collaborators from NASA, Georgia State University, Eotvos University and the University of Helsinki, have developed a 3D magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) computer simulation model that traces how magnetic energy builds up and is released to trigger Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs). The model, run on IIA's NOVA HPC facility, shows that magnetic reconnection begins slowly through a thin current sheet before intensifying into an explosive eruption of a twisted magnetic flux rope. Cross-validation with NASA's HMI and AIA solar observation data confirmed that the rate of magnetic reconnection correlates directly with the acceleration of the CME, offering a potential new tool for forecasting CME arrival and impact on Earth. The study was published in the Astrophysical Journal.

title: Building a Business-Ready India
summary: This PIB backgrounder, released around India's 80th Independence Day, compiles the government's Ease of Doing Business reforms into one narrative covering digital single-window systems, startup and MSME support, finance access, trust-based governance, market expansion and export promotion. It highlights flagship initiatives such as NSWS, Startup India, SPICe+, MCA21 V3, Udyam Registration, PMMY, CGTMSE, TReDS, Jan Vishwas Act 2026, GST 2.0, GeM, PM GatiShakti, ONDC, Export Promotion Mission, Trade Connect e-Platform and ICEGATE, with updated statistics as of mid-2026. The document frames these as building blocks of a 'business-ready India' aimed at boosting entrepreneurship, formalisation and global competitiveness.

title: NITI Aayog Report on “Key Sectors to Position India as a Global Manufacturing Hub”
summary: NITI Aayog released a report titled 'Key Sectors to Position India as a Global Manufacturing Hub', analyzing four sectors—Chemicals, Telecom & Networking Equipment, Textiles, and Solar Photovoltaic manufacturing—for their potential to boost India's manufacturing competitiveness. The study used a four-phase framework covering sector shortlisting, competitiveness assessment, international benchmarking, and actionable recommendations. It highlights key statistics such as India's textile sector contributing ~2% to GDP and employing over 45 million people, and India's solar capacity of 106 GW needing to reach 280 GW by 2030. The report is the first in a series covering 12 sectors overall, with 8 more to follow.

title: IOL launches indigenous 'GARUD' High Resolution Binoculars for civil market
summary: India Optel Limited (IOL), a Mini Ratna Category-I Defence PSU under the Department of Defence Production, has launched 'GARUD', an indigenously designed and manufactured high-resolution binocular for the civil market. Produced by Ordnance Factory, Dehradun (a unit of IOL with optical manufacturing roots dating to 1943), GARUD offers 8x magnification, a 7.6-degree field of view, ±5 diopter adjustment, weather-resistant build and weighs about 610 grams. It was launched on 13 August 2026 at DPSU Bhawan, New Delhi, in the presence of Joint Secretary (Land Systems) Dr Garima Bhagat and representatives from CAPFs, the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, and the Wildlife Society of India.

title: Over 5.63 Lakh Villages Covered with Liquid Waste Management Arrangements under SBM(G) Phase II
summary: As of 7 August 2026, 5,63,809 out of 5,86,944 villages (about 96%) have been covered with Liquid Waste Management arrangements under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II, as reported by States/UTs on the SBM(G) IMIS. A total of 42,98,194 community Grey Water Management (GWM) assets have been created nationwide, including soak pits, drainage facilities and treatment systems. This information was shared by Minister of State for Jal Shakti V. Somanna in a written reply in Lok Sabha.

title: 75% of Rural Habitations Covered with Sujal Gaon IDs under Jal Jeevan Mission Across States/UTs
summary: The Ministry of Jal Shakti informed the Lok Sabha that as of 10 August 2026, Sujal Gaon IDs have been issued to 12,67,808 out of 16,96,213 rural habitations (75%) across India under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 digital monitoring framework. These unique IDs, along with Sujalam Bharat IDs assigned to rural piped water supply schemes, form a federated Digital Public Infrastructure integrated with GIS mapping and the PM GatiShakti platform for tracking water supply infrastructure. The system enables source-to-tap mapping, asset tracking, lifecycle management and improved transparency in JJM implementation.

title: Stage set for 80th Independence Day Celebrations at Red Fort
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will lead India's 80th Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort on 15 August 2026, themed around '150 Years of Vande Mataram' and 'Yuva Shakti for Viksit Bharat@2047'. For the first time, 'Vande Mataram' will be formally rendered as part of the ceremony, alongside the traditional flag hoisting, 21-Gun Salute, Guard of Honour, and an address to the nation. The event will host around 5,000 special guests drawn from various government schemes and 2,500 NCC cadets and 'My Bharat' volunteers, with seating enclosures this year named after major Indian lakes.

title: Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Convenes Two-Day National Workshop on Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan with Participation of Over 160 Representatives from All States and UTs

ministry.name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare held a two-day National Workshop (12–13 August 2026) in New Delhi on the Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (AMB), with over 160 representatives from all States/UTs and multiple central ministries. The workshop focused on operationalising the revised AMB guidelines and the new 7×7×7 strategy, and saw the launch of a new AMB digital Application and Portal for beneficiary-level tracking, treatment monitoring and follow-up. States/UTs with strong AMB implementation performance were also recognised.

title: ISRO seized of the issue of proliferation of large number of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Satellite constellations or Satellite Internet constellations causing accumulation of Space debris and is taking all possible steps for its mitigation and prevention: Dr Jitendra Singh
summary: In a Rajya Sabha reply, Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that ISRO is actively addressing the problem of space debris accumulation caused by the proliferation of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, including large satellite internet constellations. He highlighted ISRO's 'Debris Free Space Mission' as a key initiative for Active Debris Removal (ADR) and end-of-life satellite disposal, alongside India's long-standing membership in the Inter-Agency Space Debris Coordination Committee (IADC) since 1996. He emphasized Space Situational Awareness (SSA), indigenous monitoring capabilities, and adherence to the Indian Space Policy's debris mitigation guidelines as central to long-term space sustainability.

title: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Approves Major Financial Support for Rajasthan and Telangana Under RKVY and KY
summary: Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan approved financial releases of Rs 340.59 crore for Rajasthan and Rs 265.12 crore for Telangana under the PM Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) and Krishonnati Yojana (KY), based on their annual action plans and expenditure progress. He praised Telangana's new Farmer ID and fertiliser distribution model but flagged slow spending under Oilseeds and Pulses Missions, while urging Rajasthan to focus on improving Kisan Credit Card (KCC) coverage.

title: Factual Position Regarding Media Report on Disposal of Cases by CIC

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

summary: The Central Information Commission (CIC) has clarified that a media report claiming only three appeals were disposed of in August 2026 was inaccurate; the Commission actually disposed of 768 cases up to 12 August 2026. The discrepancy arose because the Second Appeals and Complaints Portal, whose data auto-updates the CIC website, has been undergoing upgradation since 2 August 2026, leaving displayed figures frozen at 1 August 2026 levels. The CIC clarified that hearings and functioning continued normally during this period, and the upgraded portal is expected to go live from 17 August 2026.

title: Monsoon Session of Parliament Adjourns Sine Die; 12 Bills Passed by both Houses of Parliament
summary: The Monsoon Session 2026 of Parliament, which ran from 20 July to 13 August 2026 with 19 sittings over 25 days, was adjourned sine die after both Houses passed 12 Bills. Key legislation included the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill renaming the state 'Keralam', the Tribunals Reforms Bill establishing a National Tribunals Commission, and amendments to the MSME Development Act, Mines and Minerals Act, and Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act (covering Vande Mataram). The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill was referred to a Joint Committee. Lok Sabha's productivity was about 19% and Rajya Sabha's about 39%.

title: MMDR Amendment Bill, 2026
summary: The MMDR Amendment Bill, 2026 amends the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 to establish a uniform, Centre-directed fiscal framework for the mineral sector across India. It brings mineral-bearing lands under Union regulatory control, introduces a new Section 9D restricting States from imposing new taxes, cess or levies on mineral rights or mineral-bearing lands except as per Central government conditions, and invalidates pending retrospective tax demands (while not refunding already-collected amounts). The Bill has been passed by both Houses of Parliament.

title: WOMEN FRIENDLY INFRASTRUCTURE IN COURTS
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal stated that judicial infrastructure development is primarily a state responsibility, with the Centre supporting it through a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) since 1993-94. The CSS covers five components: Court Halls, residential units for judicial officers, Lawyers' Halls, toilet complexes, and digital computer rooms. He clarified that women-friendly infrastructure specifics in court halls fall under the domain of High Courts and State Governments, though CSS guidelines provide norms based on National Courts Management System (NCMS) recommendations, state practices, and CPWD standards.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: STRENGTHENING CSIR GOVERNANCE AND RESEARCH
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Science & Technology, Dr. Jitendra Singh, detailed the institutional mechanisms CSIR uses to promote research coordination, technology transfer and commercialisation. These include Business Development Groups at labs and headquarters, structured IP and licensing frameworks, incubation centres, and collaboration with ministries, states, PSUs, academia and industry.

title: Government is promoting alternate dispute resolution mechanisms including mediation
summary: The Ministry of Law and Justice informed the Rajya Sabha that the government is promoting alternate dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms, especially mediation, through legal frameworks like the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 and the Mediation Act, 2023. As of March 2026, India has 452 ADR Centres and 1,394 Mediation Centres, with 4,681 judicial officers, 10,124 lawyers, and 753 other mediators trained. NALSA, MCPC, and stakeholders like High Courts have been conducting training programs and awareness initiatives, including an Advanced Commercial Mediation Training Program and a national Mediation Conference held in March 2025.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INSPIRE-SHE SCHOLARSHIP FOR HIGHER EDUCATION
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Science & Technology Ministry clarified that the INSPIRE-SHE (Scholarship for Higher Education) scheme has not been discontinued but is being redesigned to strengthen its objectives and align with emerging priorities. Since its inception, the scheme has benefited 1,36,298 students with a total disbursement of Rs. 2,784.15 crore across states, with Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Karnataka among the top beneficiaries. The reply also detailed other overseas research support schemes: 271 INSPIRE-SHE Mentorship Grant scholars completed summer research abroad, 63 participants benefited from the WARI Fellowship (with IUSSTF), and 55 persons with disabilities pursued PhDs abroad under the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INNOVATION ECOSYSTEM
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, Minister Dr Jitendra Singh detailed the government's multi-pronged measures to strengthen India's innovation ecosystem, including the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund, Vigyan Dhara, INSPIRE, WISE-KIRAN, National Quantum Mission, Bio-RIDE and BioE3 policies, and space-sector reforms. He cited data showing GERD rose from ₹1,32,567.01 crore (0.66% of GDP) in 2019-20 to ₹2,44,767.81 crore (0.84% of GDP) in 2023-24, over 2.40 lakh DPIIT-recognised startups (more than half from Tier-II/III cities), India's 3rd rank in scientific publications, 6th in patent filings, and a jump in the Global Innovation Index from 81st (2015) to 38th (2025).

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INSPIRE PROGRAMME
summary: A written Rajya Sabha reply by MoS Dr. Jitendra Singh detailed the DST's INSPIRE Programme, which nurtures scientific talent through four components: MANAK (school students aged 10-17), SHE (undergraduate/postgraduate scholarships), Fellowship (Ph.D. support), and Faculty Fellowship (postdoctoral researchers). Five-year data (2021-22 to 2025-26) shows tens of thousands supported annually across these components, alongside targeted outreach efforts to improve inclusion of rural, remote and aspirational districts.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF E-COURTS INTEGRATED MISSION MODE PROJECT
summary: The Ministry of Law and Justice provided a Rajya Sabha update on the eCourts Mission Mode Project, currently in Phase III (2023-27), which aims to build digital, paperless and AI-enabled courts. Key achievements include 1,806 fully functional eSewa Kendras, 753.60 crore pages of court records digitised, e-filing implemented in 4,519 courts, 7,553 establishments with video conferencing facilities, and integration of all High Courts with the Interoperable Criminal Justice System (ICJS). Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal also highlighted digital literacy initiatives for litigants and lawyers, including in Andhra Pradesh.

title: The cumulative exports (merchandise & services) during April-July 2026-27 is estimated at US$ 316.42 Billion, as compared to US$ 279.63 Billion in April-July 2025-26, an estimated growth of 13.16%.
summary: India's cumulative exports (merchandise and services) during April-July 2026-27 rose 13.16% year-on-year to an estimated US$316.42 billion, up from US$279.63 billion in the same period of 2025-26. Merchandise exports grew 17.04% to US$173.78 billion, while non-petroleum exports rose 12.79% to US$143.61 billion. However, total imports grew faster at 17.28%, widening the overall trade deficit to US$49.43 billion, with merchandise trade deficit alone at US$118.60 billion, partly offset by a services trade surplus of US$69.17 billion.

title: India’s Energy Journey: Expanding Capacity, Strengthening Security
summary: This PIB backgrounder summarises India's energy sector transformation as of mid-2026, covering coal, renewables, nuclear, hydro, bio-energy, hydrogen, geothermal and petroleum sectors. Total installed power capacity has grown to about 552 GW (from 249 GW in 2014), with non-fossil sources now exceeding 54% of capacity. Key new initiatives highlighted include the ₹37,500 crore coal gasification scheme, PM-Surya Ghar rooftop solar scheme, the new Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana for floating solar with storage, GOBARdhan bioenergy scheme, SHANTI Act 2025 for nuclear private participation, National Policy on Geothermal Energy, and the Samudra Manthan offshore exploration scheme.

title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA PRESENTS SANGEET NATAK AKADEMI FELLOWSHIPS AND SANGEET NATAK AKADEMI AWARDS FOR THE YEAR 2024 AND 2025
summary: President Droupadi Murmu presented the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowships and Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards for 2024 and 2025 to eminent artists in New Delhi on 13 August 2026. In her address, she highlighted India's diverse musical, dance and folk theatre traditions, the importance of the Guru-Shishya parampara, and the need to preserve endangered folk art forms through initiatives like the Akademi's 'Kala-Diksha' programme. She described artists as guardians of collective memory and the Sangeet Natak Akademi as a key centre of India's soft power.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NUCLEAR POWER PROJECTS
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Department of Atomic Energy detailed the status of India's under-construction nuclear power projects, including RAPP-7&8, GHAVP-1&2, KAIGA-5&6, PFBR, and KKNPP-3,4,5&6, with revised costs and commissioning timelines. RAPP-7 commenced commercial operation on 15.04.2026, while other projects face delays attributed to post-Fukushima design changes, COVID-19, supply delays from Russia, and geopolitical conflicts. Upon completion, these projects are expected to add a cumulative 8,000 MW to the national grid. The reply also included five-year equity sanction, release and utilization data for each project.

title: National Celebrations on World Elephant Day 2026 held at Visakhapatnam; Gaj Gaurav Awards 2026 conferred for Exemplary Contributions to Elephant Conservation and Management

ministry.name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

summary: India held national celebrations for World Elephant Day 2026 in Visakhapatnam, led by Union MoS (EFCC) Kirti Vardhan Singh with Andhra Pradesh Deputy CM Pawan Kalyan as Guest of Honour. Gaj Gaurav Awards 2026 were conferred for exemplary contributions to elephant conservation, and a Regional Action Plan for Human-Elephant Conflict management in Southern India (Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu) was released with Rs. 500 crore central support. The event also featured the 23rd Steering Committee Meeting of Project Elephant and release of publications including '30 Giant Steps' documenting achievements since 1992.

title: PROTECTION OF MONUMENTS
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply on 13 August 2026, Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat stated that of 3,688 centrally protected ancient monuments and archaeological sites in India, 414 have reported encroachments. Uttar Pradesh (78), Tamil Nadu (72) and Karnataka (60) have the highest numbers of encroached sites. The government noted that under the AMASR Act, 1958, protection does not require land acquisition, and ASI takes action against encroachments while conducting joint surveys with revenue officials and has digitised monument boundaries on the Bhuvan Portal.

title: DIGITAL ACCESS TO CULTURAL HERITAGE
summary: The Ministry of Culture informed the Rajya Sabha that the Indian Culture Portal (ICP) has been upgraded to Version 2.0, launched in March 2026, featuring a modern secure architecture, multilingual support in 22 Indian languages via BHASHINI, an AI chatbot named 'Bharti', and Progressive Web Application functionality. The portal integrates digital resources from museums, libraries, archives and other cultural institutions under the Ministry and partner organizations into a unified discovery platform. This information was given by Union Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

title: National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Tribes
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs stated that 3,750 fellowships were awarded under the National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Tribes (NFST) over the last five years, with 750 fresh fellowships sanctioned annually for five-year research programmes. The scheme is a Central Sector Scheme with no state-wise budget allocation, and applications are invited online each year from 1 July to 30 September. Data was also shared on scholars completing research (294 in 2023-24, 156 in 2024-25, 226 in 2025-26) and on grievance redressal via CPGRAMS, which recorded 1,681 grievances disposed of with an average disposal time of 7 days between April 2021 and March 2026.

title: RETRIEVAL OF STOLEN ANTIQUITIES
summary: In a written reply to the Rajya Sabha on 13 August 2026, Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat provided a country-wise list of antiquities retrieved by India till June 2026, totaling 662 objects: 589 from the USA, 51 from Australia, 21 from the UK, and 1 from the Netherlands. He explained that retrieval is pursued case-by-case through diplomatic channels and Indian Embassies/Missions, guided by applicable national and international laws, and that no comprehensive global inventory of Indian antiquities held abroad exists.

title: “EDUCATION SUPPORT AND SCHOLARSHIP SCHEMES IN LADAKH”
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey detailed five scholarship schemes run by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs for ST students, including in the UT of Ladakh: Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, National Scholarship (Top Class), National Fellowship (NFST), and National Overseas Scholarship (NOS). He explained the Centrally Sponsored vs Central Sector nature of these schemes and their delivery mechanisms, and shared five-year beneficiary and fund-release data for Ladakh via an annexure. He also noted that an Expenditure Finance Commission appraisal for continuing these schemes (FY2026-27 to FY2030-31), including a proposal to enhance educational support, is currently underway.

title: FUNCTIONAL EMRSs
summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs informed Lok Sabha that 508 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) are currently functional across India, with state/UT-wise data provided. Odisha has 114 EMRSs sanctioned, of which 47 are functional, while Dhenkanal and Angul districts do not have blocks meeting the scheme's eligibility criteria for setting up new EMRSs. Chhattisgarh (75), Madhya Pradesh (71) and Jharkhand (51) have the highest numbers of functional schools.

title: Reservation for Limboo and Tamang Scheduled Tribes
summary: In response to a Lok Sabha question, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs stated that the issue of reservation of seats in the Sikkim Legislative Assembly for Limboo and Tamang Scheduled Tribes is sub judice before the Supreme Court in SLP (Civil) No. 26490/2023, Sikkim Gorkha Jagran Sangh vs. Union of India & Ors. The Minister of State, Shri Durgadas Uikey, cited Rule 41(2)(xviii) of the Lok Sabha's Rules of Procedure, which bars questions seeking information on matters under judicial adjudication, as the reason detailed information could not be furnished.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: MISSION MAUSAM
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Ministry of Earth Sciences provided details of Mission Mausam, a Central Sector umbrella scheme launched by the PM on 14 January 2025 with a Cabinet-approved outlay of ₹2,000 crore for 2024-26 to make India 'Weather-ready and Climate-smart'. For 2026-31, the mission will be implemented through six verticals (OBSERVE_ALL, DEVELOP, Weather_MOD, ATCOMP, FRONTIER, NEAT), with a Budget Estimate of ₹1,342.29 crore for 2026-27. The mission focuses on upgrading observation networks, high-resolution modelling, AI/ML applications, and last-mile dissemination to improve weather and climate forecasting.

title: Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu flags off Tiranga Rally under Har Ghar Tiranga Campaign 2026
summary: On 13 August 2026, Union Minister of Civil Aviation Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu flagged off a Tiranga Rally at the Ministry of Civil Aviation as part of the nationwide Har Ghar Tiranga Campaign 2026, ahead of Independence Day. The event, also attended by MoS Murlidhar Mohol, Secretary Samir Kumar Sinha, and heads of aviation bodies like AAI, DGCA, AAIB, BCAS and AERA, included inauguration of a digital video wall, rendition of Vande Mataram, a march from Udaan Bhawan to Aviation Park, and concluded with the National Anthem.

title: CASES OF FAKE ST CERTIFICATES
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply on 13 August 2026, Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey stated that while the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is the nodal ministry for notifying communities as Scheduled Tribes under Article 342 of the Constitution, the issuance and verification of ST certificates is the responsibility of State Governments/UT Administrations. He noted that complaints regarding fake ST certificates are forwarded to the concerned states/UTs, and that the Ministry has issued periodic advisories on proper verification, including recent ones on 10 March 2026 and 13 May 2026.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INDIGENIOUS WARNING SYSTEMS
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, MoS Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh detailed India's indigenous warning systems: the National Centre for Seismology monitors earthquakes 24x7 via 174 seismological observatories and is developing a pilot Earthquake Early Warning (EEW) system using P-wave detection. On cloudbursts, IMD has not conclusively studied causes of perceived increases in Himachal Pradesh but provides impact-based early warnings, and is expanding weather infrastructure (50 Doppler Weather Radars, 1008 AWSs, 6,885 rain gauges) under Mission Mausam, alongside specialized tools like the DAMINI lightning-alert app and the Mitigation Project of Lightning Safety (MPLS).

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: AI AND GEOSPATIAL TECHNOLOGIES FOR WEATHER FORECASTING
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Ministry of Earth Sciences stated it has operationalized three AI-based global weather models and developed indigenous AI/ML tools to improve weather monitoring and nowcasting of severe events like cyclones and heavy rainfall, including in Odisha. The IMD has also launched the Multi-Hazard Early Warning Decision Support System (MHEW-DSS), a public Web-GIS platform integrating geospatial technology with forecasting models for impact-based early warnings. The Ministry listed five MoUs/LoAs with Odisha-based institutions for collaborative research and reiterated that Mission Mausam, its Central Sector umbrella scheme, aims to make India a 'Weather-ready and Climate-smart Nation'.

title: PROGRESS UNDER PM-JANMAN
summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs informed Lok Sabha on progress under PM-JANMAN, a mission for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), as of 30 June 2026. As of that date, 831 Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) had been operationalised under PM-JANMAN and 474 under DAJGUA, with 15 Centres of Competence approved for Sickle Cell Disease treatment. Detailed state- and district-wise data on housing, roads, water, health, education, electrification and connectivity were also tabled, including for Maharashtra where 17 districts have PVTG population (Akola does not).

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: STRENGTHENING CLIMATE RESILIENCE AND FORECASTING CAPABILITIES
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, MoES Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh detailed India's climate monitoring and forecasting infrastructure, covering IMD's observational networks, NIOT's ocean monitoring systems, INCOIS's Coastal Vulnerability Index, and various dissemination platforms. The reply highlighted Mission Mausam, a national initiative targeting 10-15% forecast accuracy improvement by 2030 and 5km×5km resolution severe weather forecasting. It also detailed state-specific facilities in Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu, and last-mile advisory mechanisms like Panchayat Mausam Seva for farmers.

title: Skill Development Programmes for Tribals
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, Union MoS for Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey detailed skill development and livelihood programmes for tribals. Under PMJVM, 4,172 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) covering 12.48 lakh beneficiaries have been sanctioned across 28 States/UTs (₹619.17 crore), while under PM-JANMAN, 540 VDVKs covering 0.46 lakh beneficiaries have been sanctioned across 18 States/UTs (₹23.02 crore). Separately, NSTFDC has disbursed ₹1648.39 crore in concessional loans to 4,95,090 Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries over the last five years.

title: RECRUITMENT OF TEACHERS AND STAFF IN EMRSs
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, MoS for Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey stated that no representations have been received to reverse the centralized recruitment process for teachers and staff in Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs). Each full-strength EMRS (480 students, classes up to 12th) has 31 sanctioned teaching and 21 non-teaching posts, with 13 non-teaching posts earmarked for outsourcing to promote local employment. So far 9,111 staff have been recruited through the EMRS Staff Selection Examination (ESSE), and exams have been conducted for another 7,267 posts.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: STRENGTHENING LONG RANGE FORECASTING CAPABILITIES
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply on 13 August 2026, the Ministry of Earth Sciences detailed how IMD has strengthened its Long Range Forecasting capabilities using a Multi-Model Ensemble (MME) approach based on coupled dynamical climate models. This improved forecast accuracy substantially, with the average absolute error of seasonal monsoon forecasts falling from 7.8% of the Long Period Average (LPA) during 2016-2020 to 2.2% during 2021-2025. The Ministry also listed measures like network expansion, satellite integration, AI/ML tools, and the Mission Mausam Program to further improve forecasting of extreme weather events.

title: SCHEMES FOR TRIBALS IN WEST BENGAL
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, MoS Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey gave a status update on PM JANMAN scheme implementation in West Bengal as of 30 June 2026, including progress on housing, roads, water, health, nutrition, education, electrification and mobile connectivity for tribal households, with specific data for Purulia district. He also noted that Rs.12,574.70 lakh has been approved under Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA JGUA) for West Bengal, and that West Bengal has identified 495 PVTG habitations with a PVTG population of 68,720 across 4 districts and 24 blocks.

title: STATUS OF EMRSs IN WEST BENGAL
summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs informed Lok Sabha that 728 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) have been approved nationally, of which 508 are functional. In West Bengal, all 9 approved EMRSs are functional, with a total enrolment of 3,152 students in 2025-26. Alipurduar district does not meet the criteria for an EMRS as none of its blocks have the required tribal population threshold.

title: TEXT OF THE VALEDICTORY REMARKS MADE BY THE HON’BLE CHAIRMAN, RAJYA SABHA AT THE CONCLUSION OF THE 271STSESSION OF RAJYA SABHA
summary: At the conclusion of the 271st Session of the Rajya Sabha, Chairman noted that the session was marked by frequent disruptions, resulting in the House functioning for only 37 hours 49 minutes with a productivity of just 39.17%. Despite this, 12 Bills were considered and passed or returned, though only a small fraction of Starred Questions, Zero Hour Submissions and Special Mentions listed could actually be taken up. The Chairman also highlighted a two-day Orientation Programme for new Members and the introduction of new technology tools—'Vani Setu' (AI-based language translation) and 'Sadasya Setu' (mobile app for attendance and parliamentary transactions)—before adjourning the House sine die.

title: Establishment of VDVKs in Tribal Areas of Rajasthan
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply on 13 August 2026, the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs stated that 283 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) have been sanctioned under the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) across Udaipur, Salumbar, Dungarpur and Pratapgarh districts of Rajasthan, benefiting 85,349 tribal beneficiaries. These VDVKs support value addition and marketing of Minor Forest Produce and agricultural produce like wheat, dals, pickles, honey and herbal products. About ₹2,253 lakh has been released for toolkits and training, and the reply also furnished block-wise Scheduled Tribe population data (Census 2011) for eight tribal-dominated Rajasthan districts.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Vigyan TECH 2026 initiative
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Science & Technology, Dr. Jitendra Singh, informed Parliament about 'Vigyan Tech', a first-of-its-kind national initiative held on National Technology Day (11 May 2026) at BRIC-NII, New Delhi. Organized by the Department of Biotechnology, it showcased over 100 in-house technologies from 14 Ministries/Departments under a 'Whole-of-Government' approach, released a compendium ('TECH-संग्रह') of nearly 300 technologies, and saw multiple technology transfers/licensing deals and new product launches from institutions like DBT-BRIC, ICMR, CSIR, and MoFPI.

title: DISPLACEMENT OF STs IN TIGER RESERVE AREAS
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, MoS for Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey stated that relocation of villages from Core/Critical Tiger Habitats is voluntary under Section 38V(5) of the Wild Life (Protection) Act and Section 4(2) of the Forest Rights Act, 2006. He noted NCST forwards complaints on ST displacement to NTCA, financial assistance for voluntary relocation was raised from ₹10 lakh to ₹15 lakh per family in 2021, and no cases of coerced relocation have been reported by State/District level monitoring committees.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Environmental outcomes of BioE3 Policy
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Science & Technology, Dr. Jitendra Singh, detailed the environmental outcomes of the BioE3 (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment) Policy implemented by the Department of Biotechnology. The reply highlighted the 'Sujivika' digital portal for tracking biotech imports, support for bio-refinery and waste-to-value projects, and interventions like Sunderbans ecosystem restoration, alternatives to single-use plastics, and sustainable aviation fuel production. These efforts aim to reduce fossil-fuel dependency, cut greenhouse gas emissions, and advance India's circular bioeconomy and Net Zero commitments.

title: “EDUCATION AND HOUSING SCHEMES FOR STS IN KERALA”
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, MoS Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey detailed the income-eligibility limits under five central ST scholarship schemes (Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, Top Class, NFST, NOS) and NSTFDC concessional loans, along with housing support under PM JANMAN/PMAY-G for PVTGs and Kerala's own LIFE Mission and state scholarship schemes. He noted that a proposal to revise the income ceilings is under EFC appraisal for FY2026-31, pending Department of Expenditure approval.

title: Dr. Padma Gurmet Conferred UT Ladakh State Award 2025 for Exemplary Service to Sowa-Rigpa Medicine
summary: Dr. Padma Gurmet, Director of the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa (NISR), Leh, has been conferred the UT Ladakh State Award for 2025 for his contribution to preserving, promoting and developing the Sowa-Rigpa system of medicine. The award was presented by Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena at a ceremony honouring 36 individuals for the years 2022-2025 across various fields.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: PRIVATE COMPANIES IN SPACE SECTOR
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that around 440 space technology startups are registered under the DPIIT Start-up India Portal, and IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities (NGEs), including 18 startups, for various space activities. He also disclosed that private Indian companies are expected to launch 2 commercial rockets in FY 2026-27 and more than 6 in FY 2027-28, subject to IN-SPACe's launch manifest approval.

title: STRENGTHENING PM-JANMAN for PVTGs
summary: The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs informed Lok Sabha about the progress of PM-JANMAN, a mission launched by the PM for socio-economic development of 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) across 18 states and one UT. The scheme covers 11 interventions across 9 line ministries including housing, roads, water, health, education, electrification and telecom connectivity, with state-wise and ministry-wise progress data given as on 30.06.2026. Chhattisgarh has 191 sanctioned Anganwadi Centres, all operationalized, under the Ministry of Women and Child Development's Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: APPLICATIONS OF SPACE TECHNOLOGY
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Department of Space detailed major satellite missions launched in the last three years (Chandrayaan-3, Aditya-L1, XPoSat, SPADEX, NISAR, GSAT-7R) and applications of space technology in agriculture, disaster management, governance and satellite communication. It also listed high-impact use cases identified for Non-Government Entities via IN-SPACe, and outlined upcoming missions including Gaganyaan, Venus Orbiter Mission, Chandrayaan-4 and Chandrayaan-5/LUPEX.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SUPPORT TO SPACE STARTUPS
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply on 13 August 2026, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh detailed government support to India's space startups: about 440 space-tech startups are registered on the DPIIT Start-up India Portal, and IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities, of which 18 are startups. The reply listed year-wise facilitation (launch slots, testing access) provided since 2022 to startups like Skyroot, Agnikul, Pixxel, Dhruva Space and others, and disclosed IN-SPACe's fund disbursements (Seed Fund, Venture Capital Funds, Technology Adoption Fund, SBaaS, Common Technical Facilities) totalling about Rs 200 crore over five years as of 31 July 2026.

title: Implementation of Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan
summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs informed Parliament that Phase-I of the Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan has built a nationwide capacity-building framework covering about one lakh tribal villages across 30 States/UTs. Key achievements include mobilising around 15 lakh Adi Karmayogis through a cascading training structure, approving 62,187 Tribal Village Vision 2030 Plans via Gram Sabhas, and establishing 56,422 Adi Sewa Kendras as village-level single-window facilitation centres supported by Adi Karmayogi Volunteers.

title: Mobile and Internet Connectivity in Tribal Areas
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Tribal Affairs stated that the Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN), under the Department of Telecommunications, has funded mobile connectivity projects covering uncovered and tribal-dominated villages nationwide, including in Sasaram Lok Sabha Constituency (Kaimur and Rohtas districts, Bihar). As of 30 June 2026, of 3,764 total villages in the constituency, only 12 remain uncovered by 4G, and the constituency has 4,377 4G and 1,110 5G BTS towers. The reply also gave state-wise DBN/DAPST fund disbursement figures for 2021-26 (total Rs. 2,183.10 crore) and reiterated that PM-JANMAN's 4G saturation scheme aims to provide telecom connectivity to uncovered villages/habitations, including PVTG areas, within a three-year mission period.

title: STATUS OF VAN DHAN VIKAS KENDRA CLUSTERS
summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs informed Parliament that 4,712 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs), covering 12.94 lakh beneficiaries, have been sanctioned across 28 States/UTs with Rs. 642.19 crore under PMJVM and PM-JANMAN, of which 3,406 are operational. It detailed fund flow mechanisms including the Treasury Single Account system, MSP-based revolving funds for Minor Forest Produce procurement (with Rs. 2.50 crore released to Meghalaya in FY2025-26), and Chhattisgarh's cumulative Rs. 153.66 crore revolving fund since 2013-14 procuring MFPs worth Rs. 467 crore.

title: STATUS OF EMRSs
summary: The Union Minister of Tribal Affairs, Shri Jual Oram, informed the Lok Sabha that 728 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) have been approved nationwide, of which 508 are functional with 156,593 students enrolled in academic year 2025-26. In Telangana, all 23 sanctioned EMRSs are functional, enrolling 10,199 students. The statement also detailed quality-enhancement measures including smart classrooms, science/computer labs, vocational training, and cultural preservation initiatives like Tribal Corners and regional language teachers.

title: Semiconductor and AI Revolution
summary: This PIB backgrounder outlines India's dual push in semiconductors and Artificial Intelligence as India marks its 80th Independence Day. It details Semicon India 1.0 (₹76,000 crore) and the newly approved Semicon 2.0 (₹1,27,500 crore, approved July 2026) covering chip design, fabrication, packaging, equipment, materials, R&D and talent, with 12 semiconductor projects worth over ₹1.64 lakh crore approved across six states and three plants already in commercial production. It also details the IndiaAI Mission (~₹10,372 crore outlay), covering compute infrastructure (45,000+ GPUs), 20 selected indigenous foundation AI models, the AI Kosh data/model repository, 58 approved AI Centres of Excellence, Responsible AI projects, and India's global AI standing including the India AI Impact Summit 2026 and Pax Silica coalition.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: PERFORMANCE OF CPGRAMS

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

summary: In a written reply to the Rajya Sabha, the Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Dr. Jitendra Singh, provided Ministry/Department-wise data on grievances received, disposed of and pending on the CPGRAMS portal for FY 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 (as on 05-08-2026). The reply also referenced the Comprehensive Guidelines for Effective Redressal of Public Grievances issued on 23 August 2024, which prescribe a 21-day grievance redressal timeline, and noted that a Feedback Call Centre has been operational since July 2022 to independently assess citizen satisfaction with grievance resolution.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: iGOT MISSION KARMAYOGI IN WEST BENGAL

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that 90,276 civil servants from West Bengal have been onboarded onto the iGOT Karmayogi digital learning platform, though the West Bengal government has not yet signed the tripartite MoU under Mission Karmayogi. Eight draft Capacity Building Plans have been prepared for the state's priority departments, and 10,493 course completions have been recorded by West Bengal learners out of over 5,600 courses available on the platform. DoPT, the Capacity Building Commission, and Karmayogi Bharat are extending handholding support to the state, including nodal officers for coordination.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ZERO LITIGATION PENSION ECOSYSTEM

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh described government efforts to build a 'zero litigation' pension ecosystem, highlighting the 2nd National Workshop on Pension Litigation organised by the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare (DoPPW). The workshop launched a Compendium of case laws and an explanatory flyer on best practices in pension litigation, alongside 'Special Campaign 3' aimed at resolving long-pending pension grievances. The reply also referenced Pension Adalats, Inter-Ministerial Review Meetings, and the CCS (Pension) Rules 2021, which replaced the 1972 Rules and eased eligibility conditions for family pensioners including divorced and disabled daughters under Rule 50.

title: Empowering Youth, Transforming India
summary: This PIB backgrounder consolidates a decade-plus of Indian government initiatives for youth empowerment across education, skilling, employment, sports, health and civic participation, framed under the 'Amrit Peedhi' (nectar generation) working toward 'Viksit Bharat@2047'. Key highlights include the Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) platform with 2.22 crore registered youth, NEP 2020-driven education reforms, skilling missions like PMKVY and PM-SETU, sports infrastructure under Khelo India and TOPS, and health initiatives like Tele-MANAS and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan. The release presents extensive statistics comparing 2014 baselines with 2025-26 achievements to demonstrate transformation in youth development outcomes.

title: Expanding the Development Horizon
summary: A PIB backgrounder dated 13 August 2026 consolidates cumulative achievements across rural and tribal development schemes in India, covering fiscal devolution, basic services, infrastructure, livelihoods, financial inclusion, social security and targeted tribal/SC interventions. It highlights that Gram Panchayat fiscal transfers rose from ₹2.36 lakh crore under the 15th Finance Commission to ₹4.35 lakh crore under the 16th Finance Commission, and that flagship programmes such as Jal Jeevan Mission, Swachh Bharat-Grameen, PMAY-G, PMGSY, DAY-NRLM and PM-JANMAN have expanded coverage substantially since 2014-15. The document also details growth in financial inclusion (Jan Dhan, MUDRA, PM SVANidhi), social security (NPS, Atal Pension Yojana, PMJJBY/PMSBY) and tribal/SC welfare schemes (PM-JVM, PM-JUGA, PM-AJAY, EMRS, PM-YASASVI).

title: National Biodiversity Authority releases Rs. 15.52 crore ABS Proceeds from Mustard Genetic Resources

ministry.name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

summary: The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed Rs. 15.52 crore in Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) proceeds collected from M/s. Pioneer Overseas Corporation, which developed ten commercial mustard hybrid varieties using India's biological resources. Since the parental lines were sourced from intermediaries rather than identifiable farmers, an Expert Committee devised a formula distributing the funds among 26 State Biodiversity Boards and 3 Union Territory Biodiversity Councils based on each region's mustard cultivation area, using ICAR-IIRMR data. Rajasthan received the largest share (Rs. 6.43 crore, ~42% of cultivation), followed by Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. NBA has released Rs. 182.5 crore in total ABS funds to date, with Rs. 116.22 crore disbursed in the last 12 months.

title: Prime Minister shares a Sanskrit Subhashitam, highlighting determination, perseverance, and continuous effort in overcoming life's challenges
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam (verse of wisdom) on social media platform X on 13 August 2026, emphasizing determination, perseverance and courage as means to overcome life's adversities. The verse conveys that a person with resolve is never defeated by fate but achieves success through continuous effort.

title: The New Era of Indian Agriculture and Allied Sectors
summary: This PIB backgrounder presents a comprehensive overview of transformation in India's agriculture and allied sectors over the past decade, covering rising GVA, foodgrain and horticulture production, farmer welfare schemes (PM-KISAN, PMFBY, MSP, KCC), sustainable farming initiatives (Soil Health Cards, PKVY, Natural Farming Mission, PM-KUSUM), food security (NFSA, SARTHAK PDS), market linkages (e-NAM, AIF), food processing reforms (PLISFPI, PMKSY), agricultural exports, digital agriculture initiatives, and growth in livestock, dairy and fisheries sectors. It highlights India's position as the world's largest milk producer and significant growth across allied sectors like fisheries and poultry.

title: Third Meeting of Hindi Advisory Committee of Ministry of Ayush Held in New Delhi
summary: The third meeting of the Hindi Advisory Committee of the Ministry of Ayush was held in New Delhi under the chairmanship of MoS Prataprao Jadhav, attended by MPs, the Ayush Secretary, and committee members. The meeting focused on promoting the use of Hindi in official work, publications, and public outreach for the Ayush sector, and the Ministry's Hindi house journal 'Apratim Ayush' was released. Discussions centered on making Ayush-related research and schemes accessible in Hindi and other Indian languages.

title: BHARAT TAXI ROLL OUT
summary: Bharat Taxi, a cooperative-led app-based mobility platform run by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society, has been officially rolled out in Delhi-NCR, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan, with phased expansion to other cities like Lucknow, Chandigarh, Jaipur and Pune. As of 4 August 2026, it has 8.48 lakh registered drivers (Sarathis), 44.27 lakh customers, facilitates 11,106 daily rides, and has generated ₹83.70 crore in cumulative driver earnings. STCL has also signed an MoU with the West Bengal government to support its Yatri Sathi platform through driver enrolment, cooperative membership and welfare initiatives. This information was shared by Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha.

title: NEW COURSES AT TRIBHUVAN COOPERATIVE UNIVERSITY (TSU)
summary: The Ministry of Cooperation informed Rajya Sabha that Tribhuvan Sahkari University (TSU) launched three new MBA programmes in 2025-26 — Cooperative Management, Cooperative Banking and Finance, and Agribusiness Management. The university has also designed five certificate courses for professional management of cooperative societies (covering PACS, fisheries cooperatives, dairy cooperatives, DCCB board leadership, and cybersecurity for cooperative banks), to be rolled out in 2026-27. Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Amit Shah gave this information in a written reply.

title: AVAILABILITY OF QUALITY SEEDS AND FARMERS' SELF-RELIANCE THROUGH BBSSL
summary: The Ministry of Cooperation informed the Rajya Sabha that Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL), an apex cooperative body set up under the MSCS Act 2002, has introduced 124 varieties of seeds across 18 crops under the 'Bharat Beej' brand. In FY 2025-26, BBSSL produced 75,535 metric tonnes of seeds through associated farmers, and it has also launched a conservation programme for traditional indigenous seed varieties in Uttarakhand. The initiative aims to expand domestic seed production, conserve genetic resources, and reduce India's dependence on imported seeds.

title: Affordable and Accessible Healthcare for All
summary: This PIB backgrounder consolidates 12 years of India's health sector achievements, covering Ayushman Bharat's insurance coverage and digital mission, the National Health Mission's maternal-child health and disease control programmes, affordable medicine schemes like Jan Aushadhi and AMRIT, digital health tools like eSanjeevani and Tele-MANAS, and expansion of medical education infrastructure. Key figures include over 45.5 crore Ayushman Cards issued, maternal mortality declining to 87 per 1,00,000 live births, and medical colleges more than doubling from 387 to 818. The release also highlights India's exit from WHO's malaria high-burden group and integration of AYUSH systems into mainstream healthcare.

title: OBJECTIVE OF THE RANKING FRAMEWORK FOR COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES
summary: The Ministry of Cooperation informed the Rajya Sabha that a Ranking Framework for primary cooperative societies, launched on 24 January 2025, uses the National Cooperative Database (NCD) to rank societies sector-wise and State/district/block-wise across 12 sectors. State/UT Registrars of Cooperative Societies use the NCD portal to assess societies on five parameters—audit compliance, operational activities, financial performance, infrastructure, and basic identity information—out of a total of 100 marks. The framework aims to enhance transparency, efficiency, credibility, and competitiveness among cooperatives and enable dissemination of best practices from top performers.

title: BENCHMARKS FOR ORGANIC PRODUCTS OF NCOL
summary: National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) markets certified organic products under the 'Bharat Organics' brand through e-commerce, modern retail, cooperative outlets (Safal/Mother Dairy, NAFED, NCCF) and a D2C portal. It complies with National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP) standards notified by APEDA, sourcing from certified farmer groups/ICS, conducting mandatory lab testing for pesticide residues, and has signed MoUs with 28 States/UTs to promote organic cooperative farming. This was stated by Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

title: BHARAT TAXI - COOPERATIVE-MODEL MOBILITY PLATFORM
summary: Bharat Taxi, a cooperative-led digital cab-hailing platform run by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society, has been launched in Delhi-NCR, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan. As of 04.08.2026, it has 8.48 lakh registered drivers (Sarathis) and 44.27 lakh registered customers. The platform follows a zero-commission, subscription-based model with transparent fares and driver welfare measures, and receives no government financial support, as stated by Union Cooperation Minister Amit Shah in a Rajya Sabha written reply.

title: DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY IN THE COOPERATIVE SECTOR
summary: The Ministry of Cooperation has outlined multiple digital initiatives undertaken over the last three years to modernize India's cooperative sector under the 'Sahkar Se Samriddhi' vision. Key achievements include computerization of 63,686 Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) onto ERP-based software, with 54,707 declared e-PACS and over 51.58 crore digital transactions recorded. Other initiatives include computerization of Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS) offices, Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (ARDBs), the National Cooperative Database (NCD) covering 8.6 lakh cooperatives, and a Cooperative Ranking Framework launched in January 2025.

title: COORDINATION BETWEEN NCOL AND STATE COOPERATIVE FEDERATIONS
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah explained how National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) coordinates with State Cooperative Federations on organic farming, procurement, processing, branding and marketing. NCOL signs MoUs with State Cooperative Departments/Nodal Agencies, involves State Cooperative Federations, PACS, FPOs and other cooperative institutions as members/partners in the organic value chain under the 'Bharat Organics' brand, and facilitates formation of NPOP-certified Internal Control System (ICS) groups through cooperatives.

title: Safety Fencing Along 19,700 km of Railway Tracks to Prevent Trespassing and Ensure Safe Train Operations
summary: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw informed the Lok Sabha that about 19,700 km of safety fencing has been installed along railway tracks across India, including in Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, to prevent trespassing and ensure safe train operations. The Railways is also taking legal action against those involved in stone pelting on trains and running awareness programmes like OPERATION SATHI to sensitize communities living near tracks. Preventive measures include vigilance drives, sensitized train escorting parties, coordination with GRP/local police, and State Level Security Committees chaired by state DGPs.

title: Central Government Strengthens Access to Higher Education for SC Students through POST-MATRIC SCHOLARSHIP SCHEME
summary: The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment informed the Rajya Sabha that the Post-Matric Scholarship (PMS) Scheme for Scheduled Caste students aims to raise the Gross Enrollment Ratio of SC students in higher education, targeting those from the poorest households with a family income ceiling of ₹2.5 lakh per annum. The scheme is open-ended, demand-driven, and implemented via States/UTs, with Central share released after verification of data on the National Scholarship Portal. Chhattisgarh received a total of ₹203.70 crore in Central Assistance between 2021-22 and 2025-26, benefiting 4,47,482 students, with annual disbursements ranging from ₹29 crore to ₹53.60 crore.

title: RailOne App Reaches 4.76 Crore Downloads, Records 10 Lakh Daily Average Ticket Bookings
